section_summary: This section documents U.S. concern about Japanese government finance during the conflicts in Manchuria and Shanghai, including proposed foreign loans, bond refinancing, military appropriations, and external indebtedness. It contains congressional correspondence, State Department cross-reference sheets, fragments of financial reports and telegrams, and material on Japanese government-backed securities. The closing memorandum links the Seiyūkai Cabinet change to the Manchurian crisis and reviews British concern about Japan’s departure from the gold standard, yen depreciation, and renewed textile competition.

subfiles.title: Letter opposing American participation in an international loan to Japan
subfiles.to: Henry L. Stimson, Secretary of State
subfiles.about: McFadden urges the State Department to prevent American bankers from financing Japanese military activity against China.
subfiles.summary: McFadden, citing reports of an American-British international Japanese loan, asks State to forbid direct or indirect participation by American bankers, to be notified of any application, and to submit it to Congress, warning of entanglement in the Japan-China conflict.

subfiles.title: File note for telegram no. 70 on the Japanese government's financial position
subfiles.about: The note directs readers to a telegram concerning the Japanese government's financial position and the cost of military operations.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to telegram 70: Japanese government finance is a serious problem, and military costs could embarrass responsible officials.

subfiles.title: File note for despatch no. 1490 on French bank loans to Japan
subfiles.about: The note references a German despatch enclosing or discussing newspaper comment on large French bank loans to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to despatch 1490 (file 862.24/111) on large French bank loans to Japan and newspaper commentary.

subfiles.title: Government Finances—Financial Measures
subfiles.about: The report describes emergency Japanese appropriations and changes to national-bond sinking-fund deposits following dissolution of the Diet.
subfiles.summary: On January 23 the Finance Minister submitted two draft Imperial ordinances, including about 20.9 million yen for the Manchurian affair and reduced sinking-fund deposits; with the Diet dissolved and the 1932-33 budget unenacted, they needed Privy Council referral.

subfiles.title: File note for telegram no. 75 requesting a report on Japanese conditions
subfiles.about: The note references a telegram requesting a report on Japan's current economic and financial situation.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to telegram 75 (file 894.50/54) requesting a report on Japanese economic and financial conditions.

subfiles.title: Secretary of State correspondence with Thomas W. Lamont on Japanese bond financing
subfiles.to: Thomas W. Lamont, New York City
subfiles.about: The correspondence reviews Japanese government and government-backed bond transactions, including refinancing and support for the yen.
subfiles.summary: Stimson thanks Lamont for financial information: British offers to refund Japan's 1905 sterling loan, some held in the U.S., the guaranteed Taiwan Electric Power bonds, and bonds given the Yokohama Specie Bank for a J. P. Morgan loan supporting the gold-based yen.

subfiles.title: File note for telegram no. 107 on budget and Manchurian expenditures
subfiles.about: The note references a telegram on loan authorization and Japanese budget expenditures arising from the Manchurian Incident.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to telegram 107: the Diet passed a 67.5-million-yen loan bill; the Finance Minister sought 7.57 million for Manchuria in 1931-32 and 59.51 million for early 1932-33.

subfiles.title: Continuation of telegram no. 107 on budget carryovers
subfiles.about: The telegram fragment reports an Imperial ordinance carrying budget appropriations into fiscal 1932 and corrects an earlier fiscal-year label.
subfiles.summary: Neville: a March 12 Imperial ordinance carried appropriations from the current budget into fiscal 1932; he corrects the despatch 437 budget outline's dates to 1931-32; Japan's fiscal year starts April 1.

subfiles.title: File note for telegram no. 107 on Japanese foreign indebtedness
subfiles.about: The note references a telegram concerning Japanese balances and outstanding indebtedness abroad.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to telegram 107: the commercial attaché couldn't obtain exact figures on Japan's foreign balances and external liabilities.

subfiles.title: File note for despatch no. 517 on military appropriations
subfiles.about: The note references a report on Japanese appropriations for military action in Manchuria and Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to despatch 517 on appropriations for the Army, Navy and services in Manchuria and Shanghai operations.

subfiles.title: New Seiyūkai Cabinet in Japan
subfiles.about: The memorandum summarizes confidential London reporting on the Cabinet change in Japan and British economic concerns about yen depreciation.
subfiles.summary: London contacts say the Seiyukai Cabinet change was tied to Manchuria and civilian efforts to restrain the Army risked a coup; Britain fears yen depreciation and gold loss will end its textile advantage in India and China, prompting longer hours and lower wages.
